records.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
records.depth: Official proceedings metadata and abstract; not full-paper assessment
records.finding: Reported comparisons motivate retaining self-consistency and independent ensembling, and show sensitivity to protocol tuning. This does not establish failure of all communication.

records.title: Debate or Vote: Which Yields Better Decisions in Multi-Agent Large Language Models?
records.depth: Introduction, DCM definitions, Theorem2, proof and AppendixD.3.1-D.3.2 excerpt; no author-code reproduction
records.finding: Voting is a strong empirical control. The martingale theorem requires a DCM count-update model and equality of mean neighbor and focal correctness beliefs. It cannot be imported as a universal impossibility theorem for heterogeneous, evidence-asymmetric graph edits.

records.title: Demystifying Multi-Agent Debate: The Role of Confidence and Diversity
records.depth: Metadata, Sections3-5 and displayed Table1; no appendix-wide or code reproduction claim
records.finding: Diversity selection samples a larger candidate pool. Confidence expression and usage are trained with RL. These are not free uncertainty signals; importing either requires charging additional sampling or training. Their confidence target is answer correctness, distinct from conditional edge-deletion benefit.

records.title: The Cost of Consensus: Isolated Self-Correction Prevails Over Unguided Homogeneous Multi-Agent Debate
records.depth: Author arXiv metadata, abstract and HTML table of contents only; DOI venue not independently resolved
records.finding: The reported controlled study separates conformity, contextual fragility and voting loss, with isolated self-correction and unrelated-rationale controls. Its conclusions concern the studied unguided teams; they do not prove graph-conditioned credit maintenance is impossible.
